cards.explanation: The answer is by revelation from Jesus Christ. Paul, the apostle writing this letter, says, “…I received it by revelation from Jesus Christ.” He says he didn't get it from any man, and he wasn't taught it either. He also says the gospel he preached was not devised by man. No middleman, friends. Not one.

The answer is that he persecuted it and tried to destroy it. Paul doesn't hide it. He says, “…how severely I persecuted the church of God and tried to destroy it.” That's a heavy thing to admit about yourself. I think it took guts to put it in a letter. He tells it straight, and he tells it first.

The word is zealous, friends. Paul says he was “…extremely zealous for the traditions of my fathers.” That's all-in, no half measures. Me, I'm zealous about exactly one thing, and it's stamping cookies before the oven goes cold.

The answer is False. Paul says, “I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries…” His contemporaries are the people his own age. So he was ahead of many of them, not falling behind. Paul didn't need a trophy for that, friends.

The answer is Gentiles, friends. Paul says God was pleased to reveal His Son in him “…so that I might preach Him among the Gentiles…” Gentiles are people who aren't Jewish. And that's who Paul would preach to. Look at that, the man who persecuted the church is the one sent to preach Him.

The answer is False. Paul says, “…I did not rush to consult with flesh and blood…” Flesh and blood means people, so he didn't go running to ask anybody about it. Paul took another road, friends, and we'll see which one next.

The answer is Arabia and then back to Damascus. Paul says he did not go up to Jerusalem to the apostles who came before him. Instead he says, “…I went into Arabia and later returned to Damascus.” Notice the word returned, friends. He had been in Damascus before he went.

The answer is Cephas, friends. That's the name Jesus gave Simon, which means Peter (John 1:42). Paul says he went up to confer with him and stayed fifteen days. Fifteen days is a good long visit. I think that's plenty of time to talk.

The answer is True. Paul says, “But I saw none of the other apostles except James, the Lord’s brother.” So Cephas and James are the two he mentions. It's a short guest list, friends. I've had longer ones for a Tuesday batch.

The answer is the regions of Syria and Cilicia. Paul says, “Later I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.” Two regions, named right there in his own words. That's the answer straight from the letter, friends.

The answer is False. Paul says, “I was personally unknown, however, to the churches of Judea that are in Christ.” They didn't know him in person, friends. Whatever they knew came from what they heard. Next verse tells us what that was.

The word is preaching, friends. The churches hear, “The man who formerly persecuted us is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy.” Read that slow. The same man, the same faith, but now he's preaching it instead of fighting it. That's quite a turn.

The answer is that they glorify God because of Paul. Paul says, “And they glorified God because of me.” They heard the news and gave God the glory, friends. Paul doesn't say they gave him the credit. I think he wanted it that way.
